preamble: The voiced dental/alveolar stop /d/ becomes the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] under the influence of a neighbouring palatal. In Hungarian, /d/ takes the palatal place of a following gy /ɟ/ across morpheme boundaries (partial palatal assimilation, optional in careful speech) and becomes [ɟː] together with a following j.

examples.note: Partial palatal assimilation: /d/ takes the palatal place of the following gy, giving a geminate [ɟː]; the parallel t + gy gives [ɟː] in nemzetgyűlés.
Full palatal assimilation before j: /d/ becomes [ɟ] and the cluster surfaces as a geminate palatal stop.
